from solution import *
assert resolve_policy('/a/b/c','read',{'/a/b':{'read':'ALLOW'},'/a':{'*':'DENY'}})=='ALLOW'
assert resolve_policy('/a/x','read',{'/a/':{'read':'ALLOW'}})=='ALLOW'
assert resolve_policy('/x','read',{'a':{'read':'ALLOW'}}) is None
assert resolve_policy('/a/x','read',{'/a':{'read':'ALLOW'},'/a/':{'read':'DENY'}}) is None
assert resolve_policy('/x','read',{})=='DENY'
assert resolve_policy('x','read',{}) is None

prompt.text:
Implement the following API.

File contract: Return Python module solution.py.
Required API: def resolve_policy(path: str, key: str, rules: dict[str,dict[str,str]]) -> str | None
Behavior: The requested path and every rule-path key must be absolute. Normalize trailing slashes except root before lookup. Reject the entire input when two distinct raw rule paths normalize to the same path. The requested key must match ASCII [a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*. The nearest exact key wins; '*' is fallback only at the same path. Return DENY when no rule exists.
Visible example: rules /a/b|read=ALLOW and /a|*=DENY make /a/b/c read ALLOW and write DENY.

def resolve_policy(path,key,rules):
 import re
 if not re.fullmatch(r'[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*',key) or not path.startswith('/'):return None
 clean={}
 for raw,value in rules.items():
  if not raw.startswith('/'):return None
  norm=raw.rstrip('/') or '/'
  if norm in clean:return None
  clean[norm]=value
 p=path.rstrip('/') or '/'
 while True:
  r=clean.get(p,{})
  if key in r:return r[key]
  if '*' in r:return r['*']
  if p=='/':return 'DENY'
  p=p.rsplit('/',1)[0] or '/'
